seoTitle: Free EIP-191 personal_sign Message Hash Calculator
metaDescription: Compute the EIP-191 digest that personal_sign and eth_sign wallets sign, for version 0x45 or 0x00, from text or hex. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Enter a message as text or hex and choose version 0x45 (personal_sign) or 0x00 (intended validator). The tool shows the preimage and its Keccak-256 hash.
why: When a wallet asks you to sign a message, it does not sign the raw text. It prefixes it with a fixed string and the message length, hashes the result with Keccak-256 and signs that digest. Developers who verify signatures on a server or in a contract have to rebuild the same hash, and mismatches usually come from the length being counted in bytes rather than characters, or from a wrong prefix. This tool shows the exact preimage and the digest for a message, so you can compare it with what your library produced. It supports the 0x45 personal_sign form and the 0x00 form that includes a validator address. It runs in your browser and produces no signature; never paste private keys into web pages.
howTo: Enter the message and say whether it is text or hex.
Choose version 0x45 personal_sign or 0x00 validator, and enter the validator address for 0x00.
Read the preimage and the Keccak-256 hash.

faq.q: What exactly is hashed in personal_sign?
faq.a: The prefix '\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n', then the message length in bytes as decimal digits, then the message bytes. The Keccak-256 of that whole string is what the wallet signs.

faq.q: Is the length in characters or bytes?
faq.a: Bytes. A message with non-ASCII characters is longer in UTF-8 than its character count suggests, which is a common source of signature mismatches.
Data with an intended validator: the bytes 0x19 0x00, a 20-byte validator address, then the data. It ties a signature to a specific verifying contract.
No. It only computes the digest. Signing needs a private key, which you should never paste into a web page.
